questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Rarely a company has reported such consistent quarterly growth.
Rarely has a company reported such consistent quarterly growth.
Rarely does a company reported such consistent quarterly growth.
Rarely a company reports such consistent quarterly growth has.
questions.explanation: Negative adverbials like 'rarely' at the start trigger inversion: 'Rarely has a company reported...'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: It is essential that the CEO addresses the shareholders directly.
It is essential that the CEO address the shareholders directly.
It is essential that the CEO will address the shareholders directly.
It is essential that the CEO addressing the shareholders directly.
questions.explanation: After 'it is essential that', formal English uses the subjunctive (base form): 'the CEO address the shareholders.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Were it not for the sudden interest rate hike, the merger would have gone ahead.
Were it not the sudden interest rate hike, the merger would have gone ahead.
Was it not for the sudden interest rate hike, the merger would have gone ahead.
Were it not for the sudden interest rate hike, the merger will have gone ahead.
questions.explanation: 'Were it not for' is a formal inverted conditional meaning 'if it weren't for': 'Were it not for the hike, the merger would have gone ahead.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The company posted a profit, albeit a modest one.
The company posted a profit, albeit that a modest one.
The company posted a profit, albeit it a modest one.
The company posted a profit albeit for a modest one.
questions.explanation: 'Albeit' introduces a concession and is typically followed directly by a noun phrase: 'albeit a modest one.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: It was the finance director who first flagged the discrepancy in the accounts.
It was the finance director which first flagged the discrepancy in the accounts.
It was the finance director whom first flagged the discrepancy in the accounts.
It the finance director was who first flagged the discrepancy in the accounts.
questions.explanation: Cleft sentences for emphasis on a person use 'It was [person] who...': 'It was the finance director who first flagged...'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The analyst asserts that the market will rebound within a year.
The analyst asserts to that the market will rebound within a year.
The analyst asserts the market will rebounding within a year.
The analyst is assert that the market will rebound within a year.
questions.explanation: 'Assert' is followed by 'that + clause': 'asserts that the market will rebound.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Having reviewed the balance sheet, the board approved the acquisition.
Having review the balance sheet, the board approved the acquisition.
Have reviewed the balance sheet, the board approved the acquisition.
Having reviewed the balance sheet, the board approving the acquisition.
questions.explanation: 'Having + past participle' shows a completed action before the main clause: 'Having reviewed the balance sheet, the board approved...'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The vast majority of investors has welcomed the new regulations.
The vast majority of investors have welcomed the new regulations.
A vast majority of investors is welcomed the new regulations.
The vast majority of investors welcome the new regulations already.
questions.explanation: 'The majority of' + plural noun typically takes a plural verb: 'the vast majority of investors have welcomed.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The firm needn't have cut so many jobs; revenue recovered within months.
The firm needn't cut so many jobs; revenue recovered within months.
The firm didn't need have cut so many jobs; revenue recovered within months.
The firm needn't have cutting so many jobs; revenue recovered within months.
questions.explanation: 'Needn't have + past participle' expresses an unnecessary past action: 'needn't have cut so many jobs.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Not only did revenue rise, but customer satisfaction also improved.
Not only revenue rose, but customer satisfaction also improved.
Not only did revenue rise, but also customer satisfaction rose.
Not only revenue did rise, but customer satisfaction also improved.
questions.explanation: 'Not only' at the start of a clause triggers inversion: 'Not only did revenue rise, but customer satisfaction also improved.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: This is arguably the boldest expansion strategy the company has attempted.
This is arguable the boldest expansion strategy the company has attempted.
This arguably is the boldest expansion strategy the company has attempted it.
This is arguably that the boldest expansion strategy the company has attempted.
questions.explanation: 'Arguably' is an adverb used to hedge a strong claim: 'this is arguably the boldest expansion strategy.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The bank introduced a scheme whereby small businesses can access low-interest loans.
The bank introduced a scheme where small businesses can access low-interest loans by.
The bank introduced a scheme by which whereby small businesses can access loans.
The bank introduced a scheme whereby that small businesses can access loans.
questions.explanation: 'Whereby' means 'by which' and introduces a formal relative clause: 'a scheme whereby small businesses can access loans.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: So steep was the decline that the board called an emergency meeting.
So steep the decline was that the board called an emergency meeting.
So steep was the decline the board called an emergency meeting.
So steep was that the decline the board called an emergency meeting.
questions.explanation: Fronting 'so + adjective' triggers inversion: 'So steep was the decline that the board called an emergency meeting.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The acquisition of the smaller firm marked a turning point in the company's strategy.
The acquire of the smaller firm marked a turning point in the company's strategy.
The acquisition of the smaller firm mark a turning point in the company's strategy.
The acquiring the smaller firm marked a turning point in the company's strategy.
questions.explanation: Formal writing nominalizes verbs: 'acquire' becomes 'the acquisition of...'

questions.topic: Passive with modal perfect (could have been)
questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The losses could have been avoided if the risks had been properly assessed.
The losses could been avoided if the risks had been properly assessed.
The losses could have avoided if the risks had been properly assessed.
The losses could have being avoided if the risks had been properly assessed.
questions.explanation: Modal perfect passive: modal + have been + past participle: 'could have been avoided.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Some executives favor expansion; others, caution.
Some executives favor expansion; others favor, caution.
Some executives favor expansion; others is caution.
Some executives favor expansion; others favors caution.
questions.explanation: Ellipsis omits the repeated verb after a semicolon: 'others, caution' (= others favor caution).

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The startup faced fierce competition. Nevertheless, it secured a strong market share.
The startup faced fierce competition, nevertheless it secured a strong market share.
The startup faced fierce competition. Nevertheless it secured a strong market share.
The startup faced fierce competition nevertheless, it secured a strong market share.
questions.explanation: 'Nevertheless' begins a new sentence and is followed by a comma: 'faced fierce competition. Nevertheless, it secured...'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Notwithstanding the tariffs, the company expanded into new markets.
Notwithstanding of the tariffs, the company expanded into new markets.
Notwithstanding the tariffs, but the company expanded into new markets.
The tariffs notwithstanding of, the company expanded into new markets.
questions.explanation: 'Notwithstanding' means 'despite' and is followed directly by a noun phrase: 'Notwithstanding the tariffs...'

questions.question: Which is the most appropriate formal opening line for an email requesting a meeting with a potential investor?
options: I'm writing to see if you wanna grab coffee sometime.
I am writing to request a meeting at your earliest convenience to discuss a potential partnership.
Hey, can we meet? I have a business idea.
Just wondering if you're free to chat about investing.
questions.explanation: 'I am writing to request a meeting at your earliest convenience...' is a standard formal opening.

questions.question: Which is the most appropriate opening line for a formal complaint about a delayed shipment?
options: I'm super annoyed that my order still hasn't arrived.
I am writing to draw your attention to the persistent delays in the delivery of our order.
The order is delayed, and I want to complain.
I am writing to draw your attention to the persistent delays in the delivery of our order, ok.
questions.explanation: Formal complaints use precise, measured language such as 'I am writing to draw your attention to...'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The negotiators met to iron out the remaining contract disputes.
The negotiators met to iron the disputes out before the contract of.
The negotiators met to iron the disputes of before the contract out.
The negotiators met to iron out of the remaining contract disputes.
questions.explanation: 'Iron out' means 'to resolve': 'iron out the remaining contract disputes.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The proposal got rejected by the board after lengthy discussion.
The proposal got reject by the board after lengthy discussion.
The proposal got rejecting by the board after lengthy discussion.
The proposal was got rejected by the board after lengthy discussion.
questions.explanation: get + past participle: 'the proposal got rejected by the board.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: All things considered, the merger was a sound business decision.
All things consider, the merger was a sound business decision.
All things considering, the merger was a sound business decision.
All things considered that, the merger was a sound business decision.
questions.explanation: 'All things considered' is a fixed absolute participle phrase meaning 'taking everything into account.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: In light of the falling profits, the board revised its strategy.
In the light of the falling profits, the board revised its strategy, that.
Light of the falling profits, the board revised its strategy.
In light for the falling profits, the board revised its strategy.
questions.explanation: 'In light of' means 'considering': 'In light of the falling profits...'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The layoffs drew sharp criticism from employee unions.
The layoffs made sharp criticism draw from employee unions.
The layoffs gave sharp criticism draw from employee unions.
The layoffs drew of sharp criticism from employee unions.
questions.explanation: 'Draw criticism' is a fixed collocation: 'the layoffs drew sharp criticism.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The company has consistently outperformed its rivals.
The company has outperformed consistently its rivals.
Consistently the company has outperformed its rivals.
The company consistently has outperformed its rivals.
questions.explanation: Adverbs of frequency typically follow the auxiliary verb: 'has consistently outperformed.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The plan lacks a clear budget. Furthermore, its deadline is unrealistic.
The plan lacks a clear budget, furthermore its deadline is unrealistic.
The plan lacks a clear budget. Furthermore its deadline is unrealistic.
The plan lacks a clear budget furthermore, its deadline is unrealistic.
questions.explanation: 'Furthermore' begins a new sentence and is followed by a comma.

questions.question: Choose the correct question tag.
options: The board would seldom approve such a risky venture, would it?
The board would seldom approve such a risky venture, wouldn't it?
The board would seldom approve such a risky venture, doesn't it?
The board would seldom approve such a risky venture, does it?
questions.explanation: 'Seldom' makes the statement effectively negative, so the tag is positive: 'would seldom approve..., would it?'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The quarterly results were not entirely disappointing.
The quarterly results were not all disappointing entirely.
The quarterly results not were entirely disappointing.
The quarterly results were entirely not disappointing.
questions.explanation: Formal understatement places 'not' before the adverb: 'were not entirely disappointing.'

questions.topic: Advanced conditionals (Had it not been for)
questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Had it not been for the emergency loan, the company would have gone bankrupt.
Had it not for the emergency loan, the company would have gone bankrupt.
Had it not been the emergency loan, the company would have gone bankrupt.
Had it not been for the emergency loan, the company will have gone bankrupt.
questions.explanation: 'Had it not been for' means 'if it hadn't been for': 'Had it not been for the loan, the company would have gone bankrupt.'
